links.comparator_used: Base LLM without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
links.outcome: Prescription-parameter accuracy (all-correct rate) and coverage of the expert reference standard
links.effect: All-correct rate 0.948 for Retrieval-augmented LLM vs 0.494 for Base LLM. The abstract reports improved coverage but gives no separate recall figures for the RAG-only arm.
links.quote: Retrieval augmentation improved coverage and prescribing accuracy, while Physician-RAG collaborative showed the highest agreement with the expert reference standard across completeness, safety screening, prioritization, and structured prescribing quality.

links.comparator_used: Retrieval-augmented LLM workflow without physician collaboration (AI alone)
links.outcome: Prescription-parameter accuracy, recall, precision, and unsafe (AVOID) drug exposure against the expert reference standard
links.effect: All-correct rate 0.951 (Physician-RAG) vs 0.948 (RAG LLM), 0.945 (Physician) and 0.494 (Base LLM). Physician-RAG had CORE recall 1.000, overall recall 0.978, precision 0.963, the lowest case-level AVOID-hit rate (0.026), and AVOID hit@1/3/5 of 0.000/0.000/0.008.
links.quote: Prescription-parameter accuracy was highest in the Physician-RAG collaborative workflow (all-correct rate 0.951), compared with 0.948 for the Retrieval-augmented LLM workflow, 0.945 for the Physician workflow, and 0.494 for the Base LLM workflow.
